utterances.text: Thank you. A little while ago you heard the contents of the transcript which I read out, and this is what Savcic stated in the Popovic case about this document. Was he convincing when he said that the document is not authentic? It is a document that we are discussing here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think the witness is not here in the courtroom to tell us if a document is authentic by reading a portion of a testimony of another witness. It is up to the Chamber to decide if something is authentic or not at the end of the day. Please carry on. I would like to correct myself. I misspoke when I said "leave it for cross-examination." I meant re-examination of course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, if you remember, a part of the statement given by Mr. Savcic, who was the prosecutor witness in the case Popovic et al., do you remember that he said that he never set up a forward command post in Borike? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it out, you know, from transcript just a few seconds ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any other information about that? Was maybe Savcic insincere in his testimony? Did the forward command post perhaps exist? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Borike there exist forward command post of Rogatica Brigade definitely, and we know that General Savcic, or Colonel Savcic at that time, was present in Borike. And usually where the commander is present in the AOR there is forward command post, the commander is in command of entire of his unit. Whether this is officially called forward command post of particular unit or using forward command post of other unit co-operating with this particular unit, this is different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you the following and please answer that. Does General Savcic say in this transcript from the Popovic case the following: The Forward Command Post of the 65th Regiment ... Borike, 1400 hours, is something I did not set up. I did not set up this forward command post. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we see here, Colonel Savcic did say it in -- during his testimony in Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he also say that this document does not have the format of a telegram? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He says also this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. This is my question: What is missing in this document? We will see it on the screen once again - it is P125 - so you can have a look at it and assess visually what is missing there in terms of what Savcic is saying. Thank you. There, we can see it now and we shall check the authenticity of a witness who is testifying in a trial before this Tribunal. He says that the document does not have the format of a telegram. Does it have the format of a telegram? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He says what he says and this is document -- it has not the format of a telegram, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you please give us a reference where you found this portion of the testimony of Mr. Gojkovic for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps you mean Mr. Savcic, because I was reading out the testimony of Mr. Savcic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are lines 7 to 14 and then lines 16 and 17. What I asked the witness about is in lines 13 and 14. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: On the basis of what we read in Savcic's testimony and what we can see here, was this document signed by General Savcic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we see here, this document is not signed by Colonel, later on General, Savcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does he claim in his testimony that the commander of the military police never received this document? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the transcript of his testimony, he says so also -- but I think he says also that he never discussed the contents of this document or whatever, the order, you know, with the commander of the military battalion of the 65th Protection Regiment. If I correctly remember the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I will read it out and you can have a look at it. These are pages 15263, lines 1 to 5. I'm only reading the last sentence so I wouldn't read the entire transcript. "The commander of the military police never received this document and never acted in accordance with it." This is my question: If the military police commander never received this document, as his commander claims, and if he never acted in accordance with the contents of the document, does that indicate that he never, ever received this document? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is also not up to me to assess the statement and document itself and testimony of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us whether judging by the form and the contents which we just saw - and can we please put it up on the screen once again, it is 125 - so that you can have a look and I don't have to read the transcript. Thank you. We can see it now. So, should this document be part of the collection of the protection regiment or of the Drina Corps? And did you find any other documents from the protection regiment in the Drina Corps collection? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document should be in both, in Drina Corps collection and also in 65th Protection Regiment collection, if such exists, the Main Staff collection. And ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever see any document during your investigation from the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment which was a separate command unit of the Main Staff and which had its own log-book? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember seeing few documents from 65th Protection Regiment also in Drina Corps collection, not only that one but I believe there are more documents, but from the top of my head I cannot tell which one now. But I remember reviewing this -- this collection here in The Hague. I seen more documents from 65th Protection Regiment, but I don't remember the contents of these documents. But I think this is quite easy to check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In the trials Popovic et al. and in this trial, were there any other documents which were tendered and which originate from the 65th Protection Regiment? Are you aware of this as an investigator who investigated the whole matter and who testified in this trial? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware. I don't know. Is the question rather not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As a unit, as an organisational and formation unit, was the 65th Protection Regiment as a command unit of the Main Staff an integral part of the Drina Corps or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the 65th Protection Regiment was the unit of the Main Staff of VRS, but operated in the area of responsibility of Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So did the Main Staff. It was also active with all the other units attached to the Main Staff. It was also active in the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps. Are you aware of that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having units of the Main Staff in the area of responsibility of Drina Corps, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. By that logic, as they were located in the zone of the Drina Corps, should then all the documents of these units be included in the Drina Corps collection? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. It depends of what kind of document it should be, whether they -- what kind of communication did -- whether they communicate between themselves or not. They could send some documents to Drina Corps. But whether entire correspondence should be sent to Drina Corps, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show the document P233 on the right-hand side and keep the document that we have on the screen now on the left-hand side. If this is not possible, can we please just show the document P233 on the left side of the screen in B/C/S and on the right-hand side in the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, your first request -- at your first request we have these different documents now on the screen. Sometimes it takes a little time. You should be patient. Continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you see these two documents, Mr. Blaszczyk, and my question is: Were both of these documents tendered into evidence by the OTP during your testimony? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. When they were tendered into evidence, was it mentioned that the other document which we see on the right-hand side of the screen was also found in the collection of the Drina Corps, which you received in the manner that you described? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir, from whom you have this information, but this is not true. This is not document from the Drina Corps collection. I am talking about documents from the right-hand side with ERN number 04230390.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So you claim that this document was not tendered into evidence as a document found as part of the Drina Corps collection, yes or no? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this is document not from the Drina Corps collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it found there among the documents? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain about -- a little bit about this document that -- if Your Honour would like to hear it, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember receiving this document -- the copy of this document - I think it was that one - yes, I think first I received this document -- a copy of this document from the source -- our source on the field from Bosnia and Herzegovina. And later on we managed to get the original of this document from the member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, but definitely this document is not part of the Drina Corps collection. But I know this document and I received this document from this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber if you received it as a separate document or if you received it together with some other documents from the 10th Sabotage Detachment. Did you receive only this document or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I received more documents from 10th Sabotage Detachment, not many, but a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were they all entered into the database? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was the person who submitted this document and the other documents that you mentioned to you? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the original document -- I met few members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, but I think this document I received from Dragan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now show Exhibit 1D214. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please have a look at this document and on the basis of the contents and the markings, please tell us whether there are any elements on the basis of which its authenticity can be assessed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have the stamp of the unit who I believe received these documents through teleprinter, and this document was teleprinted from the Main Staff but to which unit I don't see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me help you. It says: "To the Drina Corps command," and that is a command in the command structure of units. Can you see that? Thank you. Please look at the sixth line of text from above. You see that first is the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and then the third paragraph, "to the command of the Drina Corps." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did this document pass through your hands as an investigator and as it has the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably yes, but I don't remember this document. But I see -- but based on ERN number I see that this document from Drina Corps collection. Probably I -- I seen this document in some stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we then say that this document has more elements on the basis of which it authenticity could be established than the one we had a look at previously and which was supposedly sent by the commander of the protection regiment, General Milomir Savcic? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, I can say that this document is printed out from teleprinter, and as I said, just to put a void between these two documents it's not up to me, it's rather up to Trial Chamber. But looks for me this is -- this is original document for me. But, yeah, better to have the original, of course, here, but it looks that original from some markings here and also having the stamp of the person who received this document, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please show the document 73 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is D73, marked for identification. As for the document that we still see on the screen, which the witness assessed as authentic, I would tender it into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, it is P233, perhaps marked for identification because we haven't finished the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Correction, Mr. Tolimir, I was told by the Registrar that it is not tendered yet and it will be received now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D75.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you please have a look at page 3 of this document and the signature so that I could ask you questions which I have. Please also take a look at the ERN number so that you could tell us which collection it belongs to.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, looking at ERN number, this is Drina Corps collection document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As it's a document from the Drina Corps collection, can you please have a look at the first line which says below point A: "Convoys, teams, and individuals ..." et cetera "in the Drina Corps zone of responsibility ..." Does that also indicate that this document relates to the Drina Corps? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, somehow this is related to Drina Corps, at least to the activities in Drina Corps area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please have a look at the last page now, as it contains the signature of the author of this document. Can you see in the lower right-hand corner where it says: "Captain Slavko Novakovic." The text is in Serbian and it is handwritten. Can you see the signature?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On the basis of this signature, would you say that this is an authentic document or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason not to believe that this document is authentic. I believe that this is authentic document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to tender this document into evidence as the witness has confirmed its authenticity. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think this is not a correct statement. The witness said: "I have no reason not to believe that this document is not authentic. I believe that this is authentic document." This is not a firm statement that it is in fact authentic. There is a slight difference.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have nothing against that. It's for you to decide. I suggest it be admitted into evidence on the basis of what the witness has said, I believe that it is authentic because it was entered as part of the Drina Corps collection and he himself said that this document was an integral part of that collection of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's correct. It's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The document will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My following question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment, please. We would like to receive that document number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document, Exhibit D73, is now exhibit and not marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Have I interpreted what you said correctly? You said that the documents were in Vlasenica-Bijeljina-Sokolac-Mali Zvornik; Mali Zvornik-Milanovac; Milanovac to the Republika Srpska MUP. Then they went to Banja Luka. So this is the trajectory of the documents you mentioned. Then they arrived in the Prosecution's office in Banja Luka and then in the Prosecution's office in Zagreb, and later they arrived at the Tribunal. Have I understood what you said correctly? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but from Vlasenica to Bijeljina, from Bijeljina to Sokolac, then Mali Zvornik, probably Milanovac in Serbia, and then return to RS, first to Banja Luka, Zagreb, and The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: When you entered these documents, you mentioned how they were packed, unpacked, and so on and so forth. I don't want to waste any time on that. On the basis of everything that we have seen in the course of the previous testimony and on the basis of what we have found out now, when these documents were being packed and unpacked in various places, in Banja Luka and here at the Tribunal, when they were being put into new boxes, was a record made of the way in which the documents were being repacked and on the contents of the documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is the record how the documents were repacked and not about the contents of the documents because we had no time to look at entire collection very carefully what is in. As I said, I made initial assessment in Zagreb only what is in, and then after making few copies and returning to The Hague we realised that this is Drina Corps collection, the documents from Drina Corps subordinated unit and Drina Corps itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I thought. Thank you for that addition, that information. But since these documents were repacked, would it be correct to say that they were being packed again so that is it would be easier to transport them or was it because only certain documents were documents of interest and others were returned to their initial users? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was repacked -- I mean, partially this is true that we repacked these documents to -- easier to transport these documents to The Hague -- to Zagreb and then to The Hague. But no documents were returned to initial users, what you said here. Entire collection was transported to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for answering my question. Please, would you now tell me whether the person who packed the documents was from the investigation team and did he need to have authorisation from someone in the Tribunal to perform this work? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you mean situation on the 13th of December in Banja Luka when we received this collection, is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, I have Banja Luka in mind, Zagreb as well. So could those who were involved in the transport do this of their own accord, or did they have to receive someone's approval in order to repack the documents? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In both cases there were investigators, investigator on the field office in Banja Luka at that time and me personally at the field -- ICTY field office in Zagreb and also head of the office at that time in Zagreb. And it was our decision, but of course our management in ICTY was informed about the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether the texts that were drafted were drafted here in the Tribunal or were they drafted by those who were involved in the packing of the documents and in their transport to the Tribunal, because in some cases documents have been redacted. So were documents redacted --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the question was: Were the documents or texts redacted, not drafted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But to which texts are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm interested in whether any of the contents of the documents that were brought here -- I'm interested in whether anything was redacted in those documents and whether that was done in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents itself, they are evidence. We never redacted anything from the evidence, unless it is for some reason, protection reasons, something can be redacted -- can be used in a redaction version in the court. But the documents itself were never redacted -- are never redacted here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You don't know. That's sufficient for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, that's not correct. The answer of the witness was not that he doesn't know. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, just so we don't have to play a guessing game, if General Tolimir has some reason to believe that Drina Corps documents were redacted by the OTP in their original form, then he should just put that to the witness so we don't have to, as I said, play a guessing game. If he's got something in mind, if he has a good-faith basis to put that question, then he should just put that to the witness; if he doesn't, then he should move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you got the answer of the witness, that the documents itself were never redacted. I think this is a very clear answer. This is not "I don't know." And you should deal with the request of Mr. Thayer. Have you any indication that there were documents redacted by the Prosecution? That would be very interesting for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't, Your Honour. Thank you. I said that what the investigator said was sufficient for me; that's why I asked him this question. You can check the transcript. I said that what he said was sufficient for me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This was one sentence, and the other was: "Thank you. You don't know." And that was not the correct quotation of the answer of the witness. Please carry on now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: What the witness [sic] said could also be interpreted as: You are not aware of that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with regard to the transcript I'd like to say I didn't find a single redacted page. I wanted to ask the witness about this and his answer is sufficient for me. I apologise if I caused any confusion. I apologise to Mr. Thayer in that case and also to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think this is one of the occasions when we have problems in interpretation, different ways of interpretation. We leave it like this and please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to thank Mr. Blaszczyk for the answers he's provided to the questions put to him. I'd like to thank Mr. Thayer as well. And I have no further questions for this witness. Mr. President, I would also like to thank all the interpreters. I do apologise if I read out certain segments very rapidly. My legal advisor warned me of that, but I thank you too and I think we fully understand each other. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This can happen to everybody in the courtroom. Mr. Thayer, do you have re-examination; and if yes, would you commence the re-examination after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then we have the second break now and we resume five minutes before 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any reason to believe that any of the documents contained in the Drina Corps collection were fabricated, falsified, or altered in any way?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You testified in the -- in your last appearance here that the collection or the archive was not complete. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the numbers of the few documents and if you look at the order of the number, we see that a lot of documents are missing. I can refer, for example, to the security and intelligence documents, that a lot of documents are missing from the collection. Not only from this collection, but also from other collection, collection of the Main Staff, collection in Banja Luka, actually in the possession of Ministry of Defence of RS, collection of East Bosnia Corps, a lot of documents are missing. But if we are referring to the Drina Corps collection, definitely there are lot of gaps between these documents and the dates, these particular dates, before, during, and after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you refer to the - and I'm just quoting from the transcript - the order of the number such that you could see that a lot of the documents were missing and you used the example of the security and intelligence organ documents, what do you mean when you say the order of the number?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean that each document or most of the documents has the number, his own number, and sequence number, it should be -- the following document should have the next document to the number indicating the previous document. But we see that there are a lot of gaps between the particular documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And that number that you're talking about, do we sometimes refer to that as the strictly confidential number?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially if you are referring to operational orders or security and intelligence documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, General Tolimir also asked you some questions about documents that you may have seen that were originating from the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment. First of all, who was the commander of that regiment in July 1995, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time it was Colonel Savcic, he was the commander of 65th Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The documents that you testified about seeing that originated from that unit, can you tell the Trial Chamber did that come from -- well, I'll just ask you this: Can you tell the Trial Chamber anything about the source of those documents that originated from the 65th Protection Regiment, search, RFA, or what? Were they from a collection or can you just describe to the Trial Chamber what the source of those documents was? How did we get them, if you can remember.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in this Drina Corps collection we have few documents from 65th Protection Regiment. I don't remember from the top of my head which documents they are, but I remember seeing documents. I believe that there were documents definitely from the 65th Protection Regiment, but if any document -- it's possible that the documents were seized also in various search operations done by ICTY previously in Bratunac, Zvornik, and other locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And those were of brigade headquarters or commands; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the search operation in Zvornik and Bratunac, I'm referring to the headquarters of the brigade -- of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was there any such search of the 65th Protection Regiment?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at P -- I think it's 125, the 13 July proposal from General Tolimir that we've spent a lot of time on today. General Tolimir asked you a number of questions about your conclusions as an investigator, and I just want to ask you a couple of questions concerning the document that we have before us. Do you recall what Danko Gojkovic had to say about the signature at the lower left-hand corner of this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He confirmed that this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And with the Usher's assistance I just hand up to you the original of this document. Sir, can you tell the Trial Chamber, is that an original signature or is that a photocopy of the signature identified by Mr. Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is original signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you testified about some of the limitations that you faced as an investigator in terms of trying to authenticate or investigate certain documents, this one included. I don't think there's any dispute that one of the steps the OTP took was to interview Mr. Gojkovic and you're familiar with that interview; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with his testimony before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I followed in some extent his testimony here, but not entire one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I just want to ask you a couple of quick questions and see if that -- if you can tell the Trial Chamber whether it affects your conclusion as an investigator about the authenticity of this document. At transcript page 2817 in this trial Mr. Gojkovic identified that signature, that original signature, as his own. And at page 2818 of his testimony before this Trial Chamber, he testified that the fact that he signed and wrote "delivered" on that document indicates that he actually typed it into a teleprinter and sent it. Were you aware that he testified to that effect, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And on page 2824 of the trial transcript he said - I think this is on cross-examination by General Tolimir - that that document that you have in your hands, P125, and I'll quote: "This is for me a confirmation from the other side, from my fellow teleprinter operator on the other side, who confirmed that it was well received." General Tolimir asked him again at page 2825: "Is the document of confirmation also one that was written by the typewriter or something else?" And Mr. Gojkovic answered: "Confirmation for me is the time written on the document ..." And here we see that that's 1510 hours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this part of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I think we all know and we're -- we can all agree that we don't have the teleprinter that was being used in the Rogatica Brigade, so we have this typewritten version that Mr. Gojkovic testified about receiving and then retyping into the teleprinter that we don't have. Now, General Tolimir asked you all kinds of question about how a teleprinter works and what kind of traces it would leave, but for you as an investigator, sir, can you tell the Trial Chamber how having the actual teleprinter operator who confirmed that he sent this document and identified his own original signature on it, how that affects your conclusion about its authenticity.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course after interviewing Danko Gojkovic and after hearing his testimony here in the court, my conclusion is that this is original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just so that there's no question on the record, how does it affect your conclusion about the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that after hearing the testimony of Mr. Gojkovic and having interviewed him, I can only repeat that for me this is original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in your mind as an investigator, based on your investigation, is there any doubt that Mr. Gojkovic did what he said he did, which was receive this in typed form that we have here, sent it out on a teleprinter, and received confirmation from the teleprinter operator on the other end. Do you have any doubt as an investigator that that's what happened?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not. I believe what Mr. Gojkovic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let's look at this document and its particulars. I want to look at some of the elements of P125. And if we look at the top line, it says: "Forward command post, 65th Motorised Protection Regiment, Borike at 1400 hours." Now, General Tolimir quoted to you from then Colonel Savcic, now General Savcic's, testimony, where he said that: "I didn't set up that IKM." Do you recall that, General Tolimir reading that testimony to you, that General Savcic testified that he didn't set up that forward command post?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Are you aware of what General Savcic has stated in his OTP interview and testified in Popovic about whether he was, in fact, at the forward command post in Borike on this day at this time, 1400 hours on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember his entire testimony, statement, but he confirms that he was in Borike in this period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. General Savcic couldn't have been at a command place that he hadn't established. Please, one should specify which command post. It's not a command -- it was not the command post of the protection regiment and that's being discussed. So what does the Prosecution have in mind, in fact. Could he please clarify that. Whose command post was he at? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, could you help Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. The -- this might be a little tedious, but I'll take us step by step. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you stated that you weren't entirely familiar with General Savcic's OTP statement and testimony, so I'll just take you to a couple sections here. He first says at transcript page 15246, line 7: "There were two bases. They were the Borike and Rogatica sectors where these tasks were performed ..." And he says later on at line 13: "I was in the sector of the Sjeversko village towards Boksanica, this is where I was at the forward command post of the brigade ..." Now, are you aware of a forward command post in the village of Sjeversko, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am, sir. It was called also from time to time Borike forward command post. But this place is located approximately 4 kilometres on the road from Borike. The village is called Sjeversko. In fact, Borike is visible from the place where forward command post was located, it was located at the school in Sjeversko.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we go to the next page, transcript page 15247, at line 4 we see that Colonel Savcic confirms that he was situated in Borike in July of 1995 and that he would sleep at Borike, and that General Tolimir arrived at the Borike sector. And if we look at transcript page 15249, line 10 and 9, we see Colonel Savcic again confirming that he was in the sector of Sjeversko village and then he says: "Borike is a more general and better-known term that we normally use, but to be more precise, I was in the vicinity of the village of Borike." Okay. So are you familiar with the forward command post in the Sjeversko village that Colonel Savcic here refers to as Borike?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Have you been there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've been there a few times even.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, I'm not sure if there was -- if you misspoke by quoting in lines 18 to 20 Borike is a more general and better known term ..." and then you referred -- "... to be more precise to the vicinity of the village of," again, "Borike." Perhaps you misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Indeed I did, Mr. President. He was referring to the village of Sjeversko in the first instance and I'll just get that cite back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have the impression that the witness understood you correctly and he was -- he answered your question by stating that he was in Sjeversko.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Actually, to be more precise, I didn't misquote the transcript. Let me just read the paragraph from the beginning and that will -- we can all go back and look at it later. But it's page 15249, line 9, Colonel Savcic, I think we'll all agree, is talking about Major Malinic who is in Nova Kasaba at the time. And in a couple moments I'm going to ask some questions about that, but just to give you the background: "A. He was in Nova Kasaba, and I was in the sector of Sjeversko village. Borike is a more general and better-known term that we normally use, but to be more precise, I was in the vicinity of the village of Borike."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So, sir, you've -- again you've been to this forward command post that's in the Sjeversko village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And you've told the Court that it is very close to Borike and we have Savcic noting that they're basically interchangeable terms. Now, let's look at the first line of this proposal from General Tolimir. It says: "There are over a thousand members of the former 28th Division of the so-called BiH army captured in the area of Dusanovo (Kasaba). Prisoners were under control of the military police" --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think you can wait until Mr. Thayer has finished. Then you will get the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: "... prisoners are under control of the military police battalion of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, what is your concern?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Thayer told us to look at the first line of General Tolimir. Did he mean General Savcic because this information was not given by Tolimir. So can we please correct the record so that we have in the transcript the name of the person who provided the information rather than my name. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document is clear in its reference to the proposal originating from the assistant commander for security and intelligence affairs of the VRS Main Staff. That is General Tolimir, unless he is going to dispute that fact in this trial. That is what I am referring to here as the proposal that's explicitly referred to as coming from General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, General Tolimir asked you some questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can it please be established, what is this based on, that the first sentence comes from Tolimir? Where is any relation with Tolimir here? Is Tolimir the one who is providing this information here or is it someone else? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to continue with my line of questioning if it's all the same to the Court and not waste time with what we can all see with our own eyes. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At the moment, to avoid any conflict, we are looking at a document signed by commander Lieutenant-Colonel Milomir Savcic. This is out of any dispute, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is certainly not in dispute, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And now you are trying to get some more information from the witness about the background of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I'm focusing everyone's attention on the first paragraph that refers specifically to General Tolimir's proposal. This is where it says the: "Assistant commander for security and intelligence affairs of the VRS Main Staff proposes the following measures ..." And again, I don't think General Tolimir is disputing the fact that that is him. He held that position in the VRS for the entirety of the war and did so in July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, General Tolimir asked you some questions and read you some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I do not refute any of the functions that I performed in my life. I'm proud of every one of them. But please, you cannot extract any contents from this document where someone is saying something about General Tolimir. Someone else is providing this information about Kasaba, not Tolimir. Please take this into account and please let us have Mr. Thayer correct this for the transcript because the document says something quite different. You cannot take the second paragraph as the starting point of the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think it is very clear on the transcript that Mr. Thayer is referring to a specific position and you are not disputing that you hold this position at the relevant time, and everything else will be developed now by Mr. Thayer. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, the information that's reported here in the first line, that there are over 1.000 members of the former 28th Division of the so-called BiH army captured in the area of Kasaba, are you aware from your investigations, sir, of any information that, first of all, corroborates this information in this proposal, that there were a thousand members -- over a thousand members of the Armija in Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is corroborating information we received during our investigation from various witnesses, Serbs, Bosniaks, and also Dutch Battalion members, that in Nova Kasaba soccer field there were kept about 1.000 prisoners of VRS -- I mean Muslim prisoners captured by VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the Trial Chamber has heard some of that testimony already and it's before the Trial Chamber in other forms as well. Are you familiar with any intercepts that were taken during this period of time that also confirm the information that's contained in this document, in this proposal from General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned only witnesses, but also --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think before you raise your objection. Mr. Thayer, you should be a little bit more careful by phrasing your questions. This is a document. You can draw from the document some conclusions, but you should not mention his name in this respect because it is not authenticated by Mr. Tolimir himself. Please, it's only a question of rephrasing your words. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question because the Prosecutor intends to lead the witness into saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I've expressed my concern about the way this last question was put to the witness. I think leave now Mr. Thayer conducting his re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But please, do not record in the transcript that I said this because I have not signed this document and I have not provided it. So please, if this could be corrected in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Tolimir. The transcript reflects what is happening in court and we have had now the transcript what Mr. Thayer said, your objection, my concern, everything is on the transcript and is very transparent for everybody. There is no way to correct that. Please carry on, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that there were intercepts that were taken at about this time concerning the events that are described here in this first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am, I am. I remember. I referred only to the witness statements and witness testimony, but I am aware also about intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's look at P410A and P410B, please. Actually, we can just make do with 410A. We don't need both. 410A will be the handwritten notebook version of this intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This question does not follow from the cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this question follows directly from General Tolimir's cross-examination of Mr. Blaszczyk. He has put the authenticity of this document squarely at issue. He has raised questions about Danko Gojkovic's credibility. He has quoted extensively from General Savcic's testimony. This goes directly to the issue of the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is, in my view, sufficient. Please carry on. Mr. Tolimir, I think all your responses and objections are followed. Please, what is your objection now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My objection is that this is not a discussion with Mr. Tolimir which is shown now. These are other participants, so someone who has nothing to do with this document cannot discuss about the authenticity of this document. I do not think that Mr. Blaszczyk even knows who are the participants in this particular conversation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We can judge that after having heard the answer of the witness. Please carry on, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We can see here, Mr. Blaszczyk, that in the second line there's a reference to: "I have over a thousand." And further down the participant specifies that: "They are down here at the soccer field." And again, based on your investigation of this case in the Kasaba area, was there a particular location where a large group of Muslim prisoners were being held by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the only place that this soccer field of -- this is soccer field in Nova Kasaba, the only place in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then we see a reference to a "Rade, Zoka, and others have just arrived." During the course of your investigation, sir, are you aware of anybody in particular whose nickname is Zoka?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know a few names with these names -- people with these names, but I don't know to whom it's -- the person who is talking he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at P411A -- oh, by the way, before we dispense with this document can you note what the time is of this intercept, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written here 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, may we have P411A, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. There is no date or place noted here. Could Mr. Thayer ask the witness about this, if the witness perhaps knows that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I can certainly refer everybody to 410B which is the print-out which will show the date clearly, but I don't think we need to waste further court time. I'll just note for the record that 410B is the print-out version which will bear the date of the conversation. If there are any further questions we can return to that later. But if I may continue in the time we have left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now we have here an intercept time of 1405 hours, sir. Do you see a reference in the middle of the intercept that starts with: "Bro, don't take anyone." And this is after there's a reference to the soccer field. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what does he say after that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I will send you an urgent telegram now, don't take anyone. I'll send you the telegram now and explain it to you. "Go ahead. "Secure it well and you will get it now in telegram. "Fine. "Cheers. "I will do nothing before that. "Nothing."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, 1411B [sic] will be the print-out version of this. And I can represent for the Court that that date is 13 July 1995 for both of these intercepts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please, for the record, repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: 411B, bravo, for the print-out. Now, sir, 65 ter 765, please, if we might. This is a new document that does not have a P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. How can this be evidence, something that resulted later on from a document? It says that at 1400 it was received when it was typed out, and it says that it was sent at 1400 hours. What does that have to do with this document and what does that have to do with Tolimir? Can that please be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If I may continue, Mr. President. I think that's a matter for submissions that we'll gladly make any time, but I think the timing of these intercepts and the time that's listed on P125 speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, to clarify the situation, you are not under time pressure. Therefore, we can continue with this witness tomorrow for your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I can understand that Mr. Tolimir's very interested in some questions he is raising. But, Mr. Tolimir, we have no problem with these documents. They are already admitted. They are in evidence. We have the documents already and everybody can look at it, the time, the date, and everything, and the content. So there's no reason for your concern in this respect. Mr. Thayer, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we have another intercept here. The time indicated is 1602 hours, and again I can represent that this is on the 13th of July, 1995. You see the reference to Kasaba in the first line. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: "I've got an extension down in Kasaba." And then he follows up and says: "Where Malinic's unit is." And again, sir, who is Malinic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Malinic is Zoran Malinic. They called him Zoka also. It could be Zoka. He is the commander of the military battalion of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who is Mr. Malinic's direct superior, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: His direct superior is Colonel Milomir Savcic, at that time Lieutenant-Colonel Milomir Savcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where was the headquarters of Mr. Malinic's unit in July of 1995 or at this time when this intercept was taken, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Malinic's unit -- Major Malinic's unit was located at that time in Nova Kasaba, in the school located in Nova Kasaba, just a few hundred metres from soccer field in Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then we can see that the reference is to 1500 gathered at the stadium in Kasaba. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And having had an opportunity to review these three intercepts again today, how does that correspond, first, with what you've learned through the course of your investigation from, as you said, survivors, Serb soldiers, and others; and number two, how does that correspond with what we're seeing here in this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, this confirms what we learned during our investigation, the documents, intercepts, and also the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And so as an investigator, sir, who's worked on this case for a long time, how accurate would you say, based on your investigation, this first line here is about the thousand members of the Muslim army being captured at Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure that this is correct information. We know that many people, more than 1.000 people were kept at Nova Kasaba soccer field and were captured along the road Konjevic Polje-Milici and then put on the location of Nova Kasaba soccer field.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, were you or did you become aware during the course of your investigation of a conversation over the radio telephone between Colonel Savcic and Major Malinic on the 13th of July about these over a thousand prisoners at Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was such conversation, but I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, at the transcript page 15255 of the Popovic trial, General Savcic testified about a conversation that he had with Major Malinic about those prisoners and how they should be treated. Were you aware of that testimony, sir? Does that help you refresh your recollection at all?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, Colonel Savcic testified that he had conversations with Malinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we look at transcript page 15256, do you recall what, if anything, General Savcic said - before that's broadcast - about where General Savcic was during the conversation and where General Tolimir was during that conversation?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, my first question is: Do you have any recollection of that testimony? And if you don't, then I can show you that transcript.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very roughly. I don't to the full extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's look at transcript page 15256 of General Savcic's testimony. He previously began discussing this conversation he had with Major Malinic on the 13th of July, and he is asked the question, I think by Mr. Vanderpuye at the time, and I quote: "And during your conversation with Mr. Malinic on the 13th, while you were in Borike, do you know where General Tolimir was?" And General Savcic's answer was at line 4: "I think -- in fact, I know he was somewhere there. He might even have been standing next to me. I can't remember." And the follow-up question is: "And do you know whether or not he was aware of the situation that Major Malinic was relating to you on the telephone at the time?" Savcic's answer is: "He knew. He was aware of that, if only from the conversation I had with Malinic. But whether he also had communications with other people in that broader area, I couldn't tell you. "As for the events in Nova Kasaba, he knew about that. He was around, standing next to me. But I don't know about any other communications he might have had." Who is the "he" to whom General Savcic is referring here when he says "he was standing next to me" and he knew about this conversation between General Savcic and Major Malinic?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is referring to General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I see we're out of time, Mr. President, and I do have just a couple of additional questions for tomorrow. We - I can tell the Court - also have some video we're prepared to play. We won't fill the entire day, I'm afraid. We did our best to fill the day for the week and then we lost the witnesses, as you know, and some of the cross got shortened considerably. So that's the projection for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think taking into account that we are just before the summer recess, it is always very difficult to schedule the right witnesses to fill all court time. There's no concern about that. We will see what you will provide us for tomorrow, and we -- at the end of this witness's testimony we should deal with some exhibits and exhibit numbers which have been marked for identification a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, old habits die hard. I'm sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, again you are -- have to be here tomorrow morning at 9.00, I think in Courtroom III as well, and please be reminded no contact about the content of your testimony with any party.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We adjourn and resume tomorrow in the morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
